key_insight: A validated 4D CTA pipeline can map patient-specific ascending aortic strain with good agreement to FE-based reference deformations and robust median-strain reproducibility across segmentations.
engineering_relevance: This enables noninvasive, spatially resolved assessment of aortic wall mechanics that may support risk stratification and mechanistic evaluation beyond diameter alone.
method: nnU-Net segmentation followed by optimized surface remeshing and deformable registration to estimate mesh-based strain from 4D CTA.
Finite element synthetic 4D CT sequences were used as controlled ground truth to validate registration-driven strain recovery.
Laplace-Beltrami spectral reconstruction was tested to quantify how strain reliability changes across spatial scales.
evidence_signal: Median strain showed minimal bias versus FE reference and low interobserver/nnU-Net disagreement, while 95th-percentile strain correlated inversely with diameter, AHI, and age.
watch_item: High-percentile and localized strain metrics were more sensitive to segmentation variability, so clinical use will require careful control of segmentation quality and spatial-scale choices.
paper_title: Toward Reliable Patient-Specific Aortic Strain Mapping from 4D CTA: Validation, Spectral Structure, and Clinical Potential
